meta.title: Towing and learner driving
meta.summary: You will learn how to tow a broken-down car correctly, when towing is prohibited, and what rules apply to learner driving on the roads.

lesson.h: Three ways to tow a vehicle
p: A broken-down vehicle can be towed in three ways ⟦19⟧:
list: using a flexible coupling, that is a tow rope;
using a rigid coupling, that is a rigid tow bar;
by the method of partial lifting: the front part of the towed vehicle is raised on a special support device, or it is partially loaded onto the platform of the towing vehicle.
lesson.tip: The more rigid the link between the vehicles, the lower the risk of collision when braking. That is why, in difficult conditions, the Rules allow only a rigid tow bar or partial lifting.

lesson.h: Who must be in the towed vehicle
p: When towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar, there must be a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle. The driver steers and brakes so as not to run into the towing vehicle ⟦20⟧.
Towing without a driver is allowed only on a rigid tow bar whose design ensures that, when driving in a straight line, the towed vehicle follows exactly the same path as the towing vehicle ⟦21⟧.
A tow rope that is too short leaves the driver of the towed vehicle no time to brake. One that is too long makes the vehicle start to sway from side to side, making it harder to control.
list: Tow rope: from 4 to 6 metres ⟦22⟧.
Rigid tow bar: no more than 4 metres ⟦23⟧.

p: The Rules set no other restrictions on passengers: for example, you may ride inside the towing car, or in a car being towed on a rope, next to the driver.
list: On a tow rope or rigid tow bar: in a towed bus or trolleybus, and in the load body of a towed truck ⟦24⟧.
When the front is raised or by partial lifting: in the cab and load body of the towed vehicle, and in the load body of the towing vehicle ⟦25⟧.
The steering does not work. Exception: raising the front or partial lifting ⟦26⟧.
Towing two or more vehicles at once ⟦27⟧.

The braking system does not work and the actual mass of the towed vehicle is more than half the actual mass of the towing vehicle. If it is less, towing is allowed only on a rigid tow bar or by partial lifting ⟦28⟧.
By a motorcycle without a sidecar, and towing such a motorcycle itself ⟦29⟧.
On a tow rope in black ice conditions ⟦30⟧.
Towing a moped, and towing by a moped. Exception: a trailer designed for use with a moped ⟦31⟧.
lesson.tip: Black ice plus a tow rope - prohibited. You need a rigid tow bar or partial lifting.

list: When towing motor vehicles, the speed must not exceed 50 km/h regardless of the towing method, even if the signs allow more ⟦32⟧. For comparison: a passenger car with a trailer may travel at up to 70-90 km/h outside a built-up area, depending on the road ⟦33⟧.
The towed motor vehicle has its hazard warning lights switched on ⟦34⟧.
If there are no hazard warning lights or they do not work, a warning triangle is fixed to the rear of the towed vehicle ⟦35⟧.
During hours of darkness and in poor visibility, the towed vehicle must have its position lamps on ⟦36⟧.
The tow rope is marked with at least two flags or panels measuring 200 × 200 mm, with alternating red and white diagonal stripes and a retroreflective surface (Basic Provisions, para. 12).

p: The first driving skills are learned only in an enclosed area or at a test ground ⟦37⟧. There is no flow of vehicles and pedestrians there, so a beginner's mistake will not harm anyone.
A training vehicle goes out onto the road only once the learner already has basic skills, the instructor is present, and there are no passengers in the vehicle ⟦38⟧.

lesson.h: Who may teach and what documents are needed
list: The instructor must carry a qualification certificate and a driving licence of the category they are teaching ⟦39⟧.
The learner must carry an identity document and a medical certificate confirming no contraindications to driving a vehicle ⟦40⟧.
On public roads, teaching takes place only along routes agreed with the authorised body, and in the presence of a driving instructor ⟦41⟧.
lesson.tip: A friend or relative who holds a driving licence but has no qualification certificate cannot teach you to drive on the road.

lesson.h: Where learner driving is prohibited and who is responsible for it
list: On motorways (sign 5.1) and roads with sign 5.3 “Road for motor vehicles” ⟦42⟧.
In residential zones (sign 5.38) and in residential courtyards ⟦43⟧.
During the training process, the driving instructor is treated as the driver ⟦44⟧.
It is prohibited to hand over control to a person without a driving licence; the exception is a person learning to drive ⟦45⟧.
lesson.tip: Practise parking and U-turns at a test ground, not in the yard outside your home.

p: A vehicle used for training is fitted out to meet the requirements of para. 6 of the Basic Provisions on Admitting Vehicles to Operation ⟦46⟧. A training organisation's vehicle is fitted with additional clutch and brake pedals so that the instructor can intervene at a dangerous moment, and the words “Learner vehicle” are painted on its sides and rear in the state language.

The “Learner vehicle” identification sign is fitted at the front and rear: a white equilateral triangle, apex up, with a red border and a black letter U. The side of the triangle must be at least 200 mm. On a passenger car, a double-sided sign on the roof is allowed (para. 9 of the Basic Provisions).

keyFacts: Ways to tow a vehicle: tow rope, rigid tow bar, partial lifting or raising the front ⟦1⟧.
On a tow rope or rigid tow bar, a driver is needed at the wheel of the towed vehicle ⟦2⟧.
Tow rope: 4-6 m between the vehicles; rigid tow bar: no more than 4 m ⟦3⟧.
Speed when towing: no more than 50 km/h with any method ⟦4⟧.
If the steering does not work, towing is allowed only by raising the front or partial lifting ⟦5⟧.
Towing on a tow rope is prohibited in black ice conditions; a rigid tow bar is allowed ⟦6⟧.
Brakes not working: if the mass of the towed vehicle is more than half the mass of the towing vehicle - not allowed; if less - only a rigid tow bar or partial lifting ⟦7⟧.
You must not tow two or more vehicles at once, tow with a motorcycle without a sidecar or tow such a motorcycle, or tow a moped or tow with a moped, except for a trailer designed for a moped ⟦8⟧.
The towed vehicle has its hazard warning lights switched on, and if it has none, a warning triangle is fixed to its rear ⟦9⟧.
Initial training takes place in an enclosed area or at a test ground; on the road, only with an instructor, once basic skills are in place, and without passengers ⟦10⟧.
Training on public roads follows agreed routes and takes place in the presence of a driving instructor ⟦11⟧.
Learner driving is prohibited on motorways, in residential zones and in yards ⟦12⟧.
mistakes: “The longer the rope, the safer.” The distance between the vehicles on a tow rope must be from 4 to 6 m ⟦13⟧.
Towing a vehicle with failed steering on a rope. Such a vehicle can only be towed by raising the front or by partial lifting ⟦14⟧.
Towing on a rope in black ice, “just slowly.” This is prohibited: you need a rigid tow bar or partial lifting ⟦15⟧.
Driving at normal speed while towing. The limit is 50 km/h ⟦16⟧.
Assuming that any experienced driver can teach someone to drive. You need a qualification certificate, an agreed route and a driving instructor ⟦17⟧.
Practising with a learner in a yard or on a motorway. Learner driving is prohibited there ⟦18⟧.
